rationale:
The supplied proof mixes four kinds of argument that do not depend on each other: a mass estimate for currents (Step 1), an exterior-algebra and calculus construction (Step 2(a)-(d)), real analysis using translation invariance, the fundamental theorem of calculus and Fubini (Step 3), and measure-theoretic L¹ duality (Step 4). Each is a reusable lemma with a clean Lean statement, so the proof is split into four children with no sibling dependencies.

1. mass_bound (Step 1): |Z(η)| ≤ c·M(Z) when |η| ≤ c, c > 0 and M(Z) < ∞. Its type is the same as the accepted br_la_abs_apply_le_mul_mass up to variable names. A fresh name is used so that no cross-branch history has to be integrated.
2. directional_form (Step 2(a)-(d)), specialised to the fields G = φ·h. Step 3 only uses G_t(y) = g(y − th)·h. The child gives a test m-form ω with |ω| ≤ ‖h‖|φ| and dω(x)(e) = Dφ(x)(h).
3. translation_dual (Step 3), with the Step 2(e) bound |∫u·Dφ(h)| ≤ B as its hypothesis.
4. l1_duality (Step 4): the L¹ norm is bounded by testing against C_c^∞ functions with |g| ≤ 1.

The parent keeps only the following glue:
- Step 0: the cases h = 0 and M(∂X) = ∞.
- Step 2(e): apply the hypothesis at dω, then GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply, then mass_bound with Z = ∂X and c = ‖h‖.
- Apply translation_dual with B = ‖h‖·M(∂X).toReal.
- Apply l1_duality to w = u(·+h) − u, which is integrable by Integrable.comp_add_right.
- Convert to ENNReal: ofReal_integral_eq_lintegral_ofReal, then ofReal_mul and ofReal_toReal.

subproblems.title: Evaluation of a current on a pointwise-bounded test form is bounded by sup|η| times its mass
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P, Z ∈ D_n(U) a current on U (GeometricCurrentOn U n), η ∈ D^n(U) a test form (TestFormOn U n), and c ∈ ℝ with c > 0 and covectorEuclideanNorm(η(x)) ≤ c for every x ∈ ℝ^P. If the mass M(Z) = Z.mass (= Z.massOn U) is finite, then |Z(η)| ≤ c · M(Z), where M(Z) is read as the real number M(Z).toReal.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)) (Z : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (η : TestFormOn U n) (c : ℝ), 0 < c → (∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm ((η : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n) x) ≤ c) → Z.mass ≠ ∞ → |Z η| ≤ c * Z.mass.toReal
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, Step 1 (F3), stated for a general domain U. Up to renaming of bound variables (Y, ω, C ↦ Z, η, c) this is the type of the comparator-accepted Submission.br_la_abs_apply_le_mul_mass (commit d771ac3ae563701d45563ad2e197624b3f42977f). Its Lean proof may be copied under this fresh name, and doing so was checked to compile.

Notation. For an n-covector β on ℝ^P, |β| := covectorEuclideanNorm β = √(Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P} s_I(β)), where:
- s_I(β) := (β(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)}))² if I is strictly increasing, and s_I(β) := 0 otherwise;
- e_k := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ k.
M(Z) := Z.mass, which by definition is Z.massOn U.

1. Homogeneity. For t ∈ ℝ and an n-covector β, |t • β| = |t|·|β|.
   (a) (t • β)(v) = t·β(v) for every v (ContinuousAlternatingMap.smul_apply), so s_I(t • β) = t²·s_I(β) for every I, in both cases of the definition.
   (b) Summing over I gives Σ_I s_I(t • β) = t²·Σ_I s_I(β) (Finset.mul_sum).
   (c) Since t² ≥ 0, Real.sqrt_mul gives √(t²·S) = √(t²)·√S, and √(t²) = |t| (Real.sqrt_sq_eq_abs). Hence |t • β| = |t|·|β|.

2. One-sided bound. Claim: if θ ∈ TestFormOn U n satisfies |θ(x)| ≤ c for all x, then Z(θ) ≤ c·M(Z).toReal.
   (a) θ' := c⁻¹ • θ lies in TestFormOn U n (it is a submodule), and its underlying form is x ↦ c⁻¹ • θ(x).
   (b) tsupport θ' ⊆ U, because every element of TestFormOn U n has topological support in U (the second component of its membership proof).
   (c) For every x, step 1 and c > 0 give |θ'(x)| = c⁻¹·|θ(x)| ≤ c⁻¹·c = 1.
   (d) So θ' ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n U, and GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn gives ENNReal.ofReal(Z(θ')) ≤ Z.massOn U = M(Z).
   (e) Since M(Z) ≠ ∞, ENNReal.ofReal_le_iff_le_toReal turns this into Z(θ') ≤ M(Z).toReal.
   (f) Z is linear (map_smul), so Z(θ') = c⁻¹·Z(θ). Multiplying c⁻¹·Z(θ) ≤ M(Z).toReal by c > 0 (inv_mul_le_iff₀) gives Z(θ) ≤ c·M(Z).toReal.

3. Two-sided bound.
   (a) Step 2 with θ := η gives Z(η) ≤ c·M(Z).toReal.
   (b) The underlying form of −η is x ↦ −η(x), and |−η(x)| = |η(x)| ≤ c (covectorEuclideanNorm_neg). Step 2 with θ := −η gives Z(−η) ≤ c·M(Z).toReal.
   (c) Linearity gives Z(−η) = −Z(η) (map_neg), so −Z(η) ≤ c·M(Z).toReal.
   (d) Together with (a), abs_le gives |Z(η)| ≤ c·M(Z).toReal. ∎
proof_key_steps: covectorEuclideanNorm(t • β) = |t|·covectorEuclideanNorm(β): every squared coefficient is scaled by t², and √(t²) = |t|.
c⁻¹•θ is mass-admissible whenever |θ| ≤ c. So le_massOn and ofReal_le_iff_le_toReal give c⁻¹Z(θ) ≤ M(Z).toReal.
Apply this to θ = η and θ = −η, using covectorEuclideanNorm_neg and linearity, to get |Z(η)| ≤ c·M(Z).toReal.

subproblems.title: A test m-form with coefficient norm ‖h‖|φ| whose exterior derivative evaluates to Dφ(h)
subproblems.statement: Let m ∈ ℕ, n := m + 1, φ : ℝ^n → ℝ a C^∞ function with compact support, and h ∈ ℝ^n. Then there is a test m-form ω ∈ D^m(ℝ^n) (TestFormOn univ m) with two properties. First, covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(x)) ≤ ‖h‖·|φ(x)| for every x. Second, for every x the exterior derivative dω (= exteriorDerivativeTestOn univ m ω) satisfies dω(x)(e_0, …, e_m) = Dφ(x)(h), where e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1 and Dφ(x) = fderiv ℝ φ x.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (m : ℕ) (φ : Eucl (m + 1) → ℝ) (h : Eucl (m + 1)), ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) φ → HasCompactSupport φ → ∃ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Eucl (m + 1))) m, (∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm ((ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl (m + 1)) m) x) ≤ ‖h‖ * |φ x|) ∧ ∀ x, ((exteriorDerivativeTestOn (univ : Set (Eucl (m + 1))) m ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Eucl (m + 1))) (m + 1)) : DifferentialForm (Eucl (m + 1)) (m + 1)) x (fun i => EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ)) = fderiv ℝ φ x h
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, Step 2(a)-(d), specialised to the vector fields G = φ·h, i.e. G^i = h_i φ. These are the only fields used in the parent's Step 3, which takes G_t(y) = g(y − th)·h. A complete Lean proof of exactly this statement along the steps below compiled in the decomposition scratch check, with axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

Notation.
- n := m + 1.
- e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1 for i ∈ Fin n, and e := (i ↦ e_i) : Fin n → ℝ^n.
- h_i := h i, so h = Σ_i h_i e_i.
- proj_k := EuclideanSpace.proj k, so proj_k(e_l) = 1 if k = l and 0 otherwise.
- For an m-covector β, |β| := covectorEuclideanNorm β.

1. Coordinate m-covectors. For k ∈ Fin n let dx^{(k)} := wedgeCovectors m (a ↦ proj_{k.succAbove a}), the coordinate m-covector omitting direction k.
   Claim: for all k, i ∈ Fin n, dx^{(k)}(e ∘ i.succAbove) = 1 if k = i, and 0 if k ≠ i.
   (a) By wedgeCovectors_apply_det, dx^{(k)}(e ∘ i.succAbove) = det M, where M_{a,b} := proj_{k.succAbove a}(e_{i.succAbove b}). This equals 1 if k.succAbove a = i.succAbove b and 0 otherwise.
   (b) If k = i: i.succAbove is injective, so M_{a,b} = 1 exactly when a = b. Thus M = 1 and det M = 1 (Matrix.det_one).
   (c) If k ≠ i: i ∈ {k}ᶜ = range(k.succAbove) (Fin.range_succAbove), so i = k.succAbove a₀ for some a₀. Then M_{a₀,b} = 0 for every b, because i.succAbove b ≠ i (Fin.succAbove_ne). A zero row gives det M = 0 (Matrix.det_eq_zero_of_row_eq_zero).
   (d) For m = 0 only the case k = i occurs, and M is the empty matrix with determinant 1.

2. The constant covector and the form. Put α := Σ_{k ∈ Fin n} ((−1)^k h_k) • dx^{(k)} and ω₀(y) := φ(y) • α.
   Expanding the sum (ContinuousAlternatingMap.sum_apply, smul_apply) and using step 1, α(e ∘ i.succAbove) = (−1)^i h_i for each i ∈ Fin n.
   Hence ω₀(y)(e ∘ i.succAbove) = (−1)^i h_i φ(y).

3. ω₀ is a test form on univ.
   (a) ω₀ is C^∞, as the product of the C^∞ function φ with the constant α (ContDiff.smul with contDiff_const).
   (b) ω₀(y) = 0 whenever φ(y) = 0, so ω₀ has compact support (HasCompactSupport.smul_right).
   (c) tsupport ω₀ ⊆ univ trivially.
   So ω₀ ∈ testFormOnSubmodule univ m, and ω := ⟨ω₀, _⟩ ∈ TestFormOn univ m has underlying form ω₀.

4. Strictly increasing multi-indices. Claim: the strictly increasing maps I : Fin m → Fin n are exactly the maps k.succAbove, each obtained from exactly one k.
   (a) Let I be strictly increasing, hence injective. I is not surjective: otherwise m + 1 = card(Fin n) ≤ card(Fin m) = m (Fintype.card_le_of_surjective). Pick k ∉ range I.
   (b) Then range I ⊆ {k}ᶜ = range(k.succAbove).
   (c) Both ranges are finite sets with m elements (Set.ncard_range_of_injective; k.succAbove is injective). So range I = range(k.succAbove) (Set.eq_of_subset_of_ncard_le).
   (d) Two strictly increasing maps on Fin m with the same range are equal (StrictMono.range_inj_of_wellFoundedLT, with Fin.strictMono_succAbove). Hence I = k.succAbove.
   (e) Conversely each k.succAbove is strictly increasing (Fin.strictMono_succAbove), and k ↦ k.succAbove is injective (Fin.succAbove_left_injective).
   So the finite set of strictly increasing I is the image of Fin n under the injective map k ↦ k.succAbove.

5. Norm.
   (a) By definition, |β| = √(Σ_I [I strictly increasing]·β(a ↦ EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ (I a))²), and basisFun(I a) = e_{I a} (EuclideanSpace.basisFun_apply).
   (b) Homogeneity: |t • β| = |t|·|β| for t ∈ ℝ. Each squared coefficient is multiplied by t² (Finset.mul_sum), √(t²·S) = √(t²)·√S (Real.sqrt_mul) and √(t²) = |t| (Real.sqrt_sq_eq_abs).
   (c) Reindex the sum defining |α| by step 4 (Finset.sum_filter, then Finset.sum_image with the injective map k ↦ k.succAbove). By step 2 it equals Σ_{i ∈ Fin n} (α(e ∘ i.succAbove))² = Σ_i ((−1)^i h_i)² = Σ_i h_i².
   (d) Hence |α| = √(Σ_i h_i²) = ‖h‖ (EuclideanSpace.norm_eq).
   (e) Therefore |ω₀(x)| = |φ(x) • α| = |φ(x)|·‖h‖ = ‖h‖·|φ(x)| for every x. In particular the required inequality holds.

6. Exterior derivative. By definition of exteriorDerivativeTestOn, the underlying form of exteriorDerivativeTestOn univ m ω is exteriorDerivative ω₀ (= extDeriv ω₀). Fix x.
   (a) ω₀ is differentiable at x, so exteriorDerivative_apply gives (dω₀)(x)(e) = Σ_{i ∈ Fin n} (−1)^i • D[y ↦ ω₀(y)(i.removeNth e)](x)(e_i).
   (b) By definition of Fin.removeNth, i.removeNth e = e ∘ i.succAbove. So by step 2 the map y ↦ ω₀(y)(i.removeNth e) is y ↦ ((−1)^i h_i)·φ(y).
   (c) Its derivative at x is ((−1)^i h_i)·Dφ(x) (fderiv_const_mul).
   (d) Since ((−1)^i)² = 1, (dω₀)(x)(e) = Σ_i (−1)^i (−1)^i h_i Dφ(x)(e_i) = Σ_i h_i Dφ(x)(e_i).
   (e) h = Σ_i h_i e_i, its expansion in the orthonormal basis EuclideanSpace.basisFun (OrthonormalBasis.sum_repr with basisFun_repr and basisFun_apply). Since Dφ(x) is linear, Σ_i h_i Dφ(x)(e_i) = Dφ(x)(h).

7. Steps 3, 5 and 6 show that ω ∈ TestFormOn univ m has both required properties. ∎

Remark (not needed above). The same covector is α = dx.curryLeft h, with dx := wedgeCovectors n (j ↦ proj_j): both take the value (−1)^i h_i on e ∘ i.succAbove. A related Lean computation, d(a • dx.curryLeft e_j)(x)(e) = D_j a(x), is in the comparator-accepted Submission.constancy_closed_kills_partial_derivatives (commit 469f013363eae50dbd864d795703cdc6930d8086).
proof_key_steps: wedgeCovectors_apply_det gives dx^{(k)}(e∘i.succAbove) = δ_{ki} for dx^{(k)} := wedgeCovectors m (proj ∘ k.succAbove).
α := Σ_k (−1)^k h_k dx^{(k)}, and ω := φ·α is a test form on univ with ω(y)(e∘i.succAbove) = (−1)^i h_i φ(y).
The strictly increasing maps Fin m → Fin (m+1) are exactly the i.succAbove, so covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(x)) = ‖h‖·|φ(x)|.
exteriorDerivative_apply with i.removeNth e = e∘i.succAbove gives dω(x)(e) = Σ_i h_i ∂_iφ(x) = Dφ(x)(h).

subproblems.title: Weak translation estimate from a bound on ∫ u·Dφ(h)
subproblems.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, u : ℝ^n → ℝ Lebesgue integrable, h ∈ ℝ^n and B ∈ ℝ. Assume |∫ u(x)·Dφ(x)(h) dx| ≤ B for every C^∞ compactly supported φ : ℝ^n → ℝ with |φ(x)| ≤ 1 for all x, where Dφ(x) = fderiv ℝ φ x. Then |∫ (u(x + h) − u(x))·g(x) dx| ≤ B for every C^∞ compactly supported g : ℝ^n → ℝ with |g(x)| ≤ 1 for all x.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (u : Eucl n → ℝ) (h : Eucl n) (B : ℝ), Integrable u → (∀ φ : Eucl n → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) φ → HasCompactSupport φ → (∀ x, |φ x| ≤ 1) → |∫ x, u x * fderiv ℝ φ x h| ≤ B) → ∀ g : Eucl n → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) g → HasCompactSupport g → (∀ x, |g x| ≤ 1) → |∫ x, (u (x + h) - u x) * g x| ≤ B
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, Step 3 (weak estimate). The bound of the parent's Step 2(e) for the fields G_t(y) = g(y − th)·h is taken here as the hypothesis. Indeed div G_t(y) = Dφ_t(y)(h) for φ_t(y) := g(y − th), and |φ_t| ≤ 1.

Notation. L := volume, i.e. Lebesgue measure on ℝ^n. Dg(z) := fderiv ℝ g z. Fix g as in the conclusion and let J := ∫ (u(x + h) − u(x))·g(x) dx.

1. Integrability. g is continuous (it is C^∞) and |g| ≤ 1, so g is measurable and bounded. u is integrable, and so is x ↦ u(x + h) (Integrable.comp_add_right; L is translation invariant). Hence the following are integrable (an integrable function times a bounded measurable one, e.g. Integrable.bdd_mul):
   - x ↦ u(x + h)·g(x);
   - x ↦ u(x)·g(x);
   - y ↦ u(y)·g(y − h).
   Therefore J = ∫ u(x + h) g(x) dx − ∫ u(x) g(x) dx (integral_sub).

2. Translation. Put f(y) := u(y)·g(y − h). Then f(x + h) = u(x + h)·g(x), so translation invariance (integral_add_right_eq_self) gives ∫ u(x + h) g(x) dx = ∫ f(x + h) dx = ∫ f(y) dy = ∫ u(y) g(y − h) dy. Recombining with integral_sub, J = ∫ u(y)·(g(y − h) − g(y)) dy.

3. Fundamental theorem of calculus. Fix y and let γ(t) := g(y − t•h) for t ∈ ℝ.
   (a) g is C^1, so by the chain rule (HasFDerivAt.comp_hasDerivAt) γ has derivative γ'(t) = Dg(y − t•h)(−h) = −Dg(y − t•h)(h) at every t.
   (b) γ' is continuous, hence interval integrable on [0, 1].
   (c) By intervalIntegral.integral_eq_sub_of_hasDerivAt, g(y − h) − g(y) = γ(1) − γ(0) = ∫_0^1 γ'(t) dt.
   (d) Hence g(y − h) − g(y) = −∫_0^1 Dg(y − t•h)(h) dt = −∫_{(0,1]} Dg(y − t•h)(h) dt (intervalIntegral.integral_of_le).

4. Domination and measurability.
   (a) Dg is continuous (ContDiff.continuous_fderiv) and vanishes outside the compact set tsupport g (HasCompactSupport.fderiv). So z ↦ Dg(z)(h) is continuous with compact support, hence bounded: |Dg(z)(h)| ≤ K for all z, for some K ≥ 0 (Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support).
   (b) Let ν be Lebesgue measure on ℝ restricted to (0, 1], a finite measure, and let F(y, t) := u(y)·Dg(y − t•h)(h).
   (c) F is a.e.-strongly measurable for L ⊗ ν: (y, t) ↦ u(y) is a.e.-strongly measurable (AEStronglyMeasurable.fst), and (y, t) ↦ Dg(y − t•h)(h) is continuous.
   (d) |F(y, t)| ≤ K·|u(y)|, and (y, t) ↦ K·|u(y)| is L ⊗ ν-integrable because u is integrable and ν is finite (Integrable.comp_fst). Hence F is L ⊗ ν-integrable (Integrable.mono').

5. Fubini. By steps 2 and 3, J = ∫ u(y)·(−∫ Dg(y − t•h)(h) dν(t)) dy = −∫ (∫ F(y, t) dν(t)) dy, moving the factor u(y) into the t-integral (integral_const_mul, integral_neg). By step 4 and MeasureTheory.integral_integral_swap, J = −∫ I(t) dν(t), where I(t) := ∫ u(y)·Dg(y − t•h)(h) dy.

6. Bound for each t. Fix t ∈ ℝ and set φ_t(y) := g(y − t•h).
   (a) φ_t is C^∞, as g composed with the smooth map y ↦ y − t•h.
   (b) φ_t has compact support: φ_t = g ∘ (Homeomorph.subRight (t•h)), and HasCompactSupport.comp_homeomorph applies.
   (c) |φ_t(y)| ≤ 1 for all y.
   (d) Dφ_t(y) = Dg(y − t•h) (fderiv_comp_sub), so Dφ_t(y)(h) = Dg(y − t•h)(h) and I(t) = ∫ u(y)·Dφ_t(y)(h) dy.
   (e) The hypothesis applied to φ_t gives |I(t)| ≤ B.

7. Conclusion. ν is Lebesgue measure on (0, 1], so J = −∫_0^1 I(t) dt and |J| = |∫_0^1 I(t) dt| ≤ B·|1 − 0| = B (intervalIntegral.norm_integral_le_of_norm_le_const). ∎
proof_key_steps: Translation invariance gives ∫(u(·+h) − u)g = ∫ u(y)(g(y−h) − g(y)) dy.
FTC along t ↦ g(y − th) gives g(y−h) − g(y) = −∫_0^1 Dg(y−th)(h) dt.
Domination by K|u(y)| on ℝ^n × (0,1] and Fubini give J = −∫_0^1 ∫ u(y) Dg(y−th)(h) dy dt.
For φ_t = g(·−th) ∈ C_c^∞ with |φ_t| ≤ 1, the hypothesis bounds each inner integral by B. Integrating over [0,1] gives |J| ≤ B.

subproblems.title: The L¹ norm is bounded by testing against smooth compactly supported functions with |g| ≤ 1
subproblems.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, w : ℝ^n → ℝ Lebesgue integrable and C ∈ ℝ. If ∫ w(x)·g(x) dx ≤ C for every C^∞ compactly supported g : ℝ^n → ℝ with |g(x)| ≤ 1 for all x, then ∫ |w(x)| dx ≤ C.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (w : Eucl n → ℝ) (C : ℝ), Integrable w → (∀ g : Eucl n → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) g → HasCompactSupport g → (∀ x, |g x| ≤ 1) → ∫ x, w x * g x ≤ C) → ∫ x, |w x| ≤ C
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, Step 4 (inner regularity of the finite measure |w| dL and smooth Urysohn functions), stated for an arbitrary integrable w.

One simplification relative to the parent: the outer-regular open sets O^± of the parent's Step 4(b) are not needed. The δ-thickenings alone separate K⁺ from K⁻, and the estimate needs only the inner approximation. The pointwise inequality of step 6 below replaces the parent's five-region split in Step 4(e). The construction of g in steps 3–5 was compiled in the decomposition scratch check.

Notation. L := volume on ℝ^n; integrals are against L unless stated otherwise.

1. Borel representative and the measure ν.
   (a) w is integrable, hence a.e.-strongly measurable. Let w̃ := AEStronglyMeasurable.mk w. It is strongly measurable, hence measurable, and w = w̃ L-a.e. (AEStronglyMeasurable.ae_eq_mk).
   (b) Consequently w̃ is integrable, ∫ |w| = ∫ |w̃|, and ∫ w g = ∫ w̃ g for every g (integral_congr_ae).
   (c) Let ν := L.withDensity(x ↦ ENNReal.ofReal |w̃(x)|). For every measurable E, ν(E) = ∫⁻_E ofReal|w̃| dL (withDensity_apply).
   (d) ν is a finite measure (isFiniteMeasure_withDensity_ofReal, since |w̃| has finite integral). Hence ∫_E |w̃| dL = (ν(E)).toReal for measurable E (ofReal_integral_eq_lintegral_ofReal on L.restrict E).
   (e) ν is a finite measure on ℝ^n, so the instance Measure.InnerRegularCompactLTTop is inferred and MeasurableSet.exists_isCompact_sdiff_lt applies to ν. (The old name exists_isCompact_diff_lt is deprecated.)

2. Inner approximation. Fix ε > 0.
   (a) A⁺ := {x | 0 < w̃(x)} and A⁻ := {x | w̃(x) < 0} are measurable and disjoint.
   (b) Choose compact sets K⁺ ⊆ A⁺ and K⁻ ⊆ A⁻ with ν(A⁺ \ K⁺) < ofReal ε and ν(A⁻ \ K⁻) < ofReal ε.
   (c) K⁺ ∩ K⁻ = ∅.

3. Separation. K⁺ is compact, K⁻ is closed, and they are disjoint, so Disjoint.exists_thickenings gives δ > 0 with thickening(δ, K⁺) ∩ thickening(δ, K⁻) = ∅. Put V^± := thickening(δ, K^±). Then:
   - V^± is open (isOpen_thickening);
   - K^± ⊆ V^± (self_subset_thickening, using δ > 0);
   - closure V^± ⊆ cthickening(δ, K^±) (closure_thickening_subset_cthickening), which is compact because ℝ^n is proper (IsCompact.cthickening).

4. Smooth Urysohn functions. Apply exists_contDiff_support_eq_eq_one_iff (smooth Urysohn lemma on a finite-dimensional real normed space, with smoothness ⊤) to the open set V^± and the closed set K^± ⊆ V^±. It gives a C^∞ function g^± : ℝ^n → ℝ with:
   - values in [0, 1];
   - support g^± = V^±;
   - g^±(x) = 1 for x ∈ K^±.
   Its tsupport is closure V^± ⊆ cthickening(δ, K^±), a compact set, so g^± has compact support (IsCompact.of_isClosed_subset). The parent's exists_contMDiffMap_one_nhds_of_subset_interior with model 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ^n) may be used instead.

5. The test function. Let g := g⁺ − g⁻.
   (a) g is C^∞ with compact support (ContDiff.sub, HasCompactSupport.sub).
   (b) support g⁺ ∩ support g⁻ = V⁺ ∩ V⁻ = ∅, so at each x one of g⁺(x), g⁻(x) is 0. Both take values in [0, 1], so |g(x)| ≤ 1.
   (c) If x ∈ K⁺, then g⁺(x) = 1, so x ∈ support g⁺ = V⁺, hence x ∉ V⁻ = support g⁻ and g⁻(x) = 0. So g(x) = 1.
   (d) Likewise g(x) = −1 for x ∈ K⁻.

6. Pointwise inequality. Let S := (A⁺ \ K⁺) ∪ (A⁻ \ K⁻), a measurable set. Claim: for every x, w̃(x)g(x) ≥ |w̃(x)| − 2·1_S(x)·|w̃(x)|.
   (a) If x ∈ S, the claim reads w̃(x)g(x) ≥ −|w̃(x)|, which holds because |g(x)| ≤ 1.
   (b) If x ∉ S, then x ∈ K⁺, or x ∈ K⁻, or w̃(x) = 0, because ℝ^n = A⁺ ∪ A⁻ ∪ {w̃ = 0}. In these three cases w̃(x)g(x) equals w̃(x) = |w̃(x)|, −w̃(x) = |w̃(x)|, and 0 = |w̃(x)|, respectively.

7. Integration.
   (a) Both sides of step 6 are integrable, since |w̃ g| ≤ |w̃|. integral_mono gives ∫ w̃ g ≥ ∫ |w̃| − 2∫_S |w̃| = ∫ |w̃| − 2(ν(S)).toReal.
   (b) ν(S) ≤ ν(A⁺ \ K⁺) + ν(A⁻ \ K⁻) < ofReal(2ε) (measure_union_le), so (ν(S)).toReal < 2ε.
   (c) Hence ∫ w g = ∫ w̃ g > ∫ |w̃| − 4ε = ∫ |w| − 4ε.

8. Conclusion. g is C^∞ with compact support and |g| ≤ 1, so the hypothesis gives ∫ w g ≤ C. Thus ∫ |w| < C + 4ε. Since ε > 0 is arbitrary, ∫ |w| ≤ C (le_of_forall_pos_lt_add). ∎
proof_key_steps: Take a Borel representative w̃ = w a.e. and the finite measure ν = |w̃| dL, which is inner regular for compact sets.
Choose compact K^± ⊆ {±w̃ > 0} with ν(A^± \ K^±) < ε.
Disjoint δ-thickenings and the smooth Urysohn lemma give g ∈ C_c^∞ with |g| ≤ 1, g = 1 on K⁺ and g = −1 on K⁻.
The pointwise bound w̃g ≥ |w̃| − 2·1_S|w̃| gives ∫ w g > ∫|w| − 4ε. With the hypothesis this yields ∫|w| ≤ C.
